label: S0013
statement: statement: Lemma (dynamic trie costs for prefix avoidance). Let D be a multiset of d Boolean strings of common length N, stored in a binary trie with a count at each node equal to the number of strings extending that node's prefix. Inserting or deleting one string takes O(N) time by changing the counts on its root-to-leaf path. Given this trie, an absent prefix of length m+1 can be found in O(m) time, where m=ceil(log2(max(1,d))), provided N>=m+1: at each level choose a child of minimum count, ties to 0. After i choices the live count is at most d/2^i by induction, so after m+1 choices it is less than 1 and hence zero. A trie for d strings of length N has O(dN) nodes in the worst case. Proof: each insertion/deletion visits exactly N+1 nodes; each query visits at most m+1 nodes and uses the stored exact counts; the halving induction proves the selected leaf prefix has count zero.

structure.lemma: Let f: {0,1}^N -> {0,1}, 0<t<N, M_t the 2^t x 2^(N-t) matrix M_t[a,b]=f(a,b), F any field, D_t = number of distinct rows of M_t. Then (i) rank_F(M_t) <= D_t; (ii) any deterministic streaming machine whose state after reading prefix a takes D_t distinct values (one per row class) with S state bits satisfies D_t <= 2^S; hence S >= log2 rank_F(M_t). Proof: (i) the rows span a space of dimension rank_F(M_t), and a spanning set can be chosen from the distinct rows, so rank <= D_t. (ii) rows with different contents must have different states, since their outputs differ on some suffix, so there are at least D_t distinct states and therefore at least ceil(log2 D_t) bits; by (i), D_t >= rank_F(M_t). Scope: exact, all N, all fields F; log-loss only (rank alone gives no bit lower bound); no claim of P != NP progress.

structure.lemma: Exact width for one cut (Myhill-Nerode, classical). Let f: {0,1}^N -> {0,1}, 0<t<N, and M_t[a,b]=f(a,b) for a in {0,1}^t, b in {0,1}^(N-t). Let D_t = number of distinct rows of M_t. Proof: rows with distinct contents must have distinct states, because some suffix separates them, so at least D_t states are needed. Conversely, the states can be taken to be the D_t distinct row classes, so D_t states suffice. This replaces the rank-based route: D_t is exact, not a log-loss proxy. structure.lemma: DEPTH-2 SIZE LEMMA (repair of the refuted depth-2 test). For every f on n>=1 variables: f has a DNF with |f^-1(1)| terms and a CNF with |f^-1(0)| clauses, so min(DNF terms, CNF clauses) <= 2^(n-1). Tight for parity_n: any term with k<n literals is satisfied by points of both parities, so it is not an implicant; every DNF for parity_n uses only full minterms and needs 2^(n-1) terms (dually for CNF). Consequence: the naive depth-2 size measure (terms or clauses) cannot exceed 2^(n-1), so a separation in K12-D2 needs a different measure (wires, fan-in, or a restricted class). label: S0009
statement: LEMMA R: Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, t real, s = |supp w| >= 1. Let S contain each coordinate independently with probability p <= 1/8, z uniform on fixed coordinates. Then P[gate [w.x >= t] non-constant in x_S] <= C_M p sqrt(n), C_M = sqrt(2)(M/2+2)+4. Proof: j = |S cap supp|, W = sum over S of |w_i| <= M j, N = s - j. Given S the gate is non-constant iff X = sum over fixed support w_i z_i lies in a half-open window of length W, so j >= 1 is needed. Case 1<=j<=s/2: N >= s/2 >= 1, all fixed weights are nonzero integers, so Erdos-Littlewood-Offord (open intervals of length 2 contain at most binom(N, floor(N/2)) sums, and binom(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N)) gives P_z <= (Mj/2+2)/sqrt(s/2). With 1[j>=1] <= j and E j = ps, this part is <= sqrt(2)(M/2+2) p sqrt(s) <= sqrt(2)(M/2+2) p sqrt(n). Case j > s/2 (s >= 2, 4p <= 1/2): P <= binom(s, ceil(s/2)) p^{ceil(s/2)} <= (4p)^{s/2} <= 4p; for s = 1 it is p. Summing gives the claim. Scope: integer weights bounded by constant M; C_M depends on M.

label: S0010
statement: LEMMA S-P1-WIN (window form of Littlewood-Offord). Let a_1..a_k be nonzero integers and let W be a window of W consecutive integers {a, a+1, ..., a+W-1}. Then #{x in {0,1}^k : sum_i a_i x_i in W} <= ceil(W/2) * C(k, floor(k/2)); equivalently Pr_x[sum_i a_i x_i in W] <= ceil(W/2) * C(k, floor(k/2)) / 2^k. Proof: all |a_i| >= 1, so Erdős' 1945 Littlewood-Offord bound applies: every open interval of length 2 contains at most C(k, floor(k/2)) of the 2^k subset sums sum_i a_i x_i (assignments counted with multiplicity). For each pair of consecutive integers {b, b+1}, the open interval (b-1/2, b+3/2) has length 2 and contains exactly those two integers, hence at most C(k, floor(k/2)) assignments have sum b or b+1. A window of W integers partitions into floor(W/2) such pairs plus, if W is odd, one singleton; the singleton is bounded by the same interval-of-length-2 bound. Summing over the pairs gives ceil(W/2) * C(k, floor(k/2)). This fixes only the window-probability term in the bounded-weight restriction bound; it does not by itself close G0001/G0004/G0007/G0009, because the restriction count k <= C m L/sqrt(n) and the weight reduction from polynomial to bounded weights remain open.

General statement is the cited Erdős theorem applied to integer windows, not new mathematics.

label: S0013
statement: REPAIR (random thresholds). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, let c in Z be fixed, let S subset [n] contain each i independently with probability p, and let t be uniform on [-R, R] independent of S. Put mn = c + sum over i in S of min(w_i, 0) and mx = c + sum over i in S of max(w_i, 0). Claim: the gate y -> [c + sum_{i in S} w_i y_i >= t] on y in {0,1}^S is non-constant iff mn < t <= mx. Proof: the sum takes values in [mn, mx] and attains both endpoints; the gate is constant iff t <= mn (always 1) or t > mx (always 0). Given S, P_t(mn < t <= mx) <= (mx - mn)/(2R) because the interval has length mx - mn and t has density 1/(2R). Also mx - mn = sum over i in S of |w_i| <= M|S|. Taking expectation over S with E|S| = pn gives P(non-constant) <= M p n / (2R). With R = sqrt(n): P(non-constant) <= (M/2) p sqrt(n). This holds for every fixed c and every fixed x on the fixed variables, so it is an exact statement with constant M/2 and no assumption p <= 1/8.

structure.gap: The repair is for RANDOM thresholds only. It does not give H1 for the adversarial CTW gates, where the threshold is part of the circuit. The next step is to find a variant that keeps the thresholds fixed but takes x uniform on the fixed variables, and to prove an anticoncentration bound for the fixed-part sum (Erdos-Littlewood-Offord type) in that setting.

statement: CLAIMED (session R1023, unreviewed). Proof: the gate is non-constant iff Z = sum_{i in F} w_i x_i lies in the set of l consecutive integers {t-mx, ..., t-mn-1}, where mx, mn are the max and min of the alive sum. Erdos (1945): any open interval of length 2 contains at most binom(N, floor(N/2)) of the 2^N subset sums of N reals with |a_i| >= 1, so P(Z in open interval of length 2) <= binom(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N). label: S0017
statement: LEMMA (bounded integer weights, exact scope). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, let N be its support, s = |N|, and let t in Z be arbitrary. Each variable is alive (free) independently with probability p; each non-alive variable is fixed to an independent uniform bit z_i. Let g(x) = [w.x >= t]. Then E[ g is non-constant over the free variables ] <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(s) <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(n). PROOF. Fix the alive set A, let j = |A ∩ N|, b = s - j, and let c = sum over fixed i in N of w_i z_i. Put mx = sum over i in A of max(w_i,0), mn = sum over i in A of min(w_i,0), and W_A = mx - mn = sum over i in A of |w_i| <= M*j. Zero-weight variables affect neither c nor the window. g is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c in [t-mx, t-mn), a half-open interval containing exactly W_A integers. Since c is a uniform subset sum of b reals of absolute value >= 1: writing the signed sum as (sum a_i + sum eps_i a_i)/2 shows that an interval of length 1 in c is an open interval of length 2 in the signed sums. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord then gives at most C(b, floor(b/2)) subsets per such interval. The W_A integers of the window give disjoint intervals (k-1/2, k+1/2), so #{subsets with c in the window} <= W_A * C(b, floor(b/2)). Using C(b, floor(b/2)) / 2^b <= 1/sqrt(b) for b >= 1, we get P(non-constant | A) <= min(1, W_A/sqrt(b)) whenever b >= 1; and P <= 1 always. AVERAGING. Case j <= s/2: then b >= s/2 >= 1 for s >= 2 (s = 1 with j = 0 has W_A = 0, probability 0). Here P(non-constant | A) <= M*j / sqrt(s/2) = sqrt(2)*M*j/sqrt(s), and E[j * 1{j <= s/2}] <= E[j] = p*s, so this case contributes at most sqrt(2)*M*p*sqrt(s). Case j > s/2 (this includes b = 0): by Markov P(j > s/2) <= E[j]/(s/2) = 2p, and P <= 1 contributes at most 2p. Summing: E <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2)*p*sqrt(s). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary threshold t, arbitrary n and p in [0,1]; the bound is per gate, so it also holds for the average over a family of gates.

Each variable is alive (free) independently with probability p; each non-alive variable is fixed to an independent uniform bit z_i. Let g(x) = [w.x >= t]. Then E[ g is non-constant over the free variables ] <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(s) <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2) * p * sqrt(n). PROOF. Fix the alive set A, let j = |A ∩ N|, b = s - j, and let c = sum over fixed i in N of w_i z_i. Put mx = sum over i in A of max(w_i,0), mn = sum over i in A of min(w_i,0), and W_A = mx - mn = sum over i in A of |w_i| <= M*j. Zero-weight variables affect neither c nor the window. g is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c in [t-mx, t-mn), a half-open interval containing exactly W_A integers. Since c is a uniform subset sum of b reals of absolute value >= 1: writing the signed sum as (sum a_i + sum eps_i a_i)/2 shows that an interval of length 1 in c is an open interval of length 2 in the signed sums. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord then gives at most C(b, floor(b/2)) subsets per such interval. The W_A integers of the window give disjoint intervals (k-1/2, k+1/2), so #{subsets with c in the window} <= W_A * C(b, floor(b/2)). Using C(b, floor(b/2)) / 2^b <= 1/sqrt(b) for b >= 1, we get P(non-constant | A) <= min(1, W_A/sqrt(b)) whenever b >= 1; and P <= 1 always. AVERAGING. Case j <= s/2: then b >= s/2 >= 1 for s >= 2 (s = 1 with j = 0 has W_A = 0, probability 0). Here P(non-constant | A) <= M*j / sqrt(s/2) = sqrt(2)*M*j/sqrt(s), and E[j * 1{j <= s/2}] <= E[j] = p*s, so this case contributes at most sqrt(2)*M*p*sqrt(s). Case j > s/2 (this includes b = 0): by Markov P(j > s/2) <= E[j]/(s/2) = 2p, and P <= 1 contributes at most 2p. Summing: E <= (sqrt(2)*M + 2)*p*sqrt(s). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary threshold t, arbitrary n and p in [0,1]; the bound is per gate, so it also holds for the average over a family of gates.

label: S0018
statement: LEMMA (fixed threshold, exact scope). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= M, t in Z fixed, S subset [n] with |S| = L, F = [n] minus S, x uniform on {0,1}^F, N = #{i in F : w_i != 0} >= 1, and l = sum over i in S of |w_i| (so l <= M L). Then P_x[ y -> [sum_{S} w_i y_i + sum_{F} w_i x_i >= t] is non-constant on {0,1}^S ] <= l / sqrt(N) <= M L / sqrt(N). PROOF. Let mx = sum_S max(w_i,0), mn = sum_S min(w_i,0), so mx - mn = l, and let c(x) = sum_F w_i x_i. The map y -> sum_S w_i y_i has min mn and max mx. Hence the function is non-constant iff mn + c < t <= mx + c, i.e. c lies in the half-open window [t - mx, t - mn), which contains exactly l integers. Zero-weight variables in F do not affect c. Let a_1..a_N be the nonzero F-weights, |a_i| >= 1. For an integer k, c = k iff sum_i a_i(2x_i - 1) = 2k - sum_i a_i, so c in (k - 1/2, k + 1/2) is an open interval of length 2 for the signed sums sum_i a_i e_i with e_i in {+1,-1}. Erdos (1945) Littlewood-Offord gives at most C(N, floor(N/2)) sign vectors per such interval. Hence #{x : c = k} <= C(N, floor(N/2)) for each integer k, and the bad count is at most l * C(N, floor(N/2)). Dividing by 2^N and using C(N, floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N) gives P <= l/sqrt(N). QED. Scope: integer weights, |w_i| <= M, arbitrary t, L, N >= 1. The bound l/sqrt(N) is proved; the sharper form (l/2 + 1)/sqrt(N) recorded in the lemma field is NOT proved here (only checked on exhaustive small cases with 0 violations: cm-363acd5f2b13434c, cm-71b683ac18654739).

label: S0019
statement: CLAIMED (session R1023, own proof, unreviewed). Let a = |S intersect supp(w)|, N = s - a. A gate is non-constant only if a >= 1. Given S, non-constancy means the fixed sum Z lies in l = sum over S of |w_i| <= M a consecutive integers. For each integer k, the subsets with sum k form an antichain after flipping signs (Sperner), so P(Z = k) <= binom(N, floor(N/2))/2^N <= 1/sqrt(N). Hence P_x[non-constant | S] <= M a / sqrt(N). Case s >= 2L: a <= L <= s/2, so N >= s/2 and P <= M a sqrt(2/s); E[a] = sL/n gives P <= sqrt2 M L sqrt(s)/n <= sqrt2 M L/sqrt(n). Case s < 2L: P <= E[a] = sL/n < 2L^2/n <= 2L/sqrt(n) <= 2ML/sqrt(n). Both cases give 2ML/sqrt(n).

structure.refuted_approach: The step citing Erdos 1945 as an open interval of length 2 for {0,1}-subset sums is false: N=1, a=1 gives sums 0 and 1, both in (-0.5, 1.5). Length 2 is the +-1 form; for {0,1}-sums the correct length is 1.

label: S0033
statement: LEMMA (window count, nonzero integer weights; repair of S0011). Let k >= 1, a = (a_1..a_k) with every a_i in Z\{0}, and let W >= 1 be an integer. For any integer t, #{x in {0,1}^k : sum_i a_i x_i in [t, t+W-1]} <= W * C(k, floor(k/2)). PROOF. (1) Let P = {i : a_i > 0}, N = {i : a_i < 0}. Substitute y_i = x_i for i in P and y_i = 1 - x_i for i in N; this is a bijection of {0,1}^k. Since a_i x_i = a_i + |a_i| y_i for i in N, the sum equals C + sum_i |a_i| y_i for a constant C, so the count equals #{y : sum_i |a_i| y_i in [t', t'+W-1]} with t' = t - C. (2) Fix an integer v and let G_v = {J subset [k] : sum_{i in J} |a_i| = v}. If A is a proper subset of B and all |a_i| > 0, then sum_A < sum_B, so G_v is an antichain. By Sperner's theorem |G_v| <= C(k, floor(k/2)). The assignments y with sum |a_i| y_i = v correspond bijectively to G_v. (3) The window [t', t'+W-1] contains W integers, so the count is at most sum over those W values v of |G_v| <= W * C(k, floor(k/2)). QED. SCOPE: all weights nonzero. A zero weight multiplies the count by 2 and can be removed by factoring out 2^(#zero weights); for k' nonzero weights the bound then reads 2^(k-k') * W * C(k', floor(k'/2)). Verification: exhaustive over all a in {-3..3}\{0}^k, k<=5, W<=4, all integer t: 488,940 tests, 0 violations (cm-c2db9270a7c947aa); earlier independent random run cm-a4221c13235f4359, 245,528 trials, 0 violations. Control: the old bound ceil(W/2)*C(k,floor(k/2)) fails 7,722 times, as predicted. Status: bookkeeping for the window count. It does not close G0001, G0003 or G0004 and is not P vs NP progress.

label: S0001
statement: PROOF. (i) The Laplacian eigenvalues of the circulant on n=2k are 3 - 2cos(2pi j/n) - (-1)^j for j=0..n-1. j=0 gives 0. Odd j give 4 - 2cos(2pi j/n) >= 2. Even j != 0 give 2 - 2cos(2pi j/n), minimised at j=2 or j=n-2, with value 2 - 2cos(2pi/k) = 4 sin^2(pi/k) < 2. Hence lambda_2 = 4 sin^2(pi/k). (ii) Label u_i = i and v_i = i+k for 0 <= i <= k-1. Edges: rungs u_i v_i; rails u_i u_{i+1} and v_i v_{i+1} for i <= k-2; twisted edges u_{k-1} v_0 and v_{k-1} u_0. For k even take j = k/2 - 1 and S = {u_0..u_j, v_0..v_j}, |S| = k; the edges leaving S are u_j u_{j+1}, v_j v_{j+1}, u_{k-1} v_0, v_{k-1} u_0, so 4. For k odd take j = (k-3)/2 and S = {u_0..u_{j+1}, v_0..v_j}, |S| = 2j+3 = k; the edges leaving S are the rung u_{j+1} v_{j+1}, rails u_{j+1} u_{j+2} and v_j v_{j+1}, and the twisted edges u_{k-1} v_0 and v_{k-1} u_0, so 5. Hand checks: k=3, S={0,1,3} in Z_6 has 5 leaving edges; k=4, S={0,1,2,3} in Z_8 has 4.

(ii) There is S with |S| = k and exactly 4 edges leaving S when k is even, and exactly 5 when k is odd; so M2k has a balanced cut of width at most 5. Scope: exact for all k >= 3 (closed form); part (ii) gives one cut per k. This is a side lemma: it closes no recorded obligation and does not bound r on the arc cut.

label: S0004
statement: STATEMENT (restates S0015). G=(V,E), E = A disjoint-union B, D = V(A) cap V(B) nonempty, Ao = V(A)\V(B), Bo = V(B)\V(A); Sigma as defined in S0015. If G has a perfect matching M0 and vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles C_1..C_r, each containing an A-edge and a B-edge, then |Sigma| >= 2^r. PROOF. (1) For S subset of [r], M_S = M0 xor (union of C_i, i in S) is a perfect matching. a_S = M_S cap A covers Ao (every edge at an Ao-vertex is in A), so it is a valid row; b_S = M_S cap B covers Bo, so it is a valid column. (2) Each D-vertex is covered by exactly one M_S-edge, lying in A or in B, so sigma(b_S) = D minus sigma(a_S) and sigma(a_S) in Sigma. (3) For v in D let sigma_v(M) = 1 iff the M-edge at v lies in A. Vertices off the cycles keep their M0 value. For v on C_i, the M_S-edge at v is the M0-edge when i not in S and the other C_i-edge at v when i in S. Hence sigma(M_S) = sigma(M0) XOR (XOR over i in S of f_i) over GF(2), where f_i is the indicator of D-vertices on C_i whose two cycle edges have different labels. (4) C_i contains both an A-edge and a B-edge, so the cyclic label sequence changes at least twice; each change happens at a vertex incident to both an A-edge and a B-edge, i.e. a vertex of D on C_i. So f_i is nonzero. The supports of the f_i are disjoint (cycles are vertex-disjoint), so the f_i are GF(2)-linearly independent. Therefore S -> sigma(M_S) is injective on the 2^r subsets, all images lie in Sigma, and |Sigma| >= 2^r. QED. SCOPE: exact for any graph and any packing as stated. GAP: none found by hand check; the definition of Sigma is taken from S0015 and not re-read. STATUS: CLAIMED. Not reviewed. Authored in a claude-haiku-5-5 session, so it needs a SURVIVED_REVIEW from another model family. Evidence: cm-cbd09ec2d4ad44f4 (own code, n=6, 209 labelled graphs, 0 violations, min |Sigma| = 5 when r >= 2). That check is small (n = 6 only) and does not test n = 8 or larger.

label: S0005
statement: Switching bound (crossing form): let G be cubic bipartite with balanced cut (A,B), M0 a perfect matching, and C_1..C_r pairwise vertex-disjoint M0-alternating cycles, each containing at least one cut edge. For S subset of [r], let M_S = M0 xor (union of C_i for i in S) and sig(M) = M cap E(A,B). Then each M_S is a perfect matching, S -> sig(M_S) is injective, and |Sigma| >= 2^r. Proof: (1) flipping a vertex-disjoint alternating cycle preserves a perfect matching. (2) Let P_i = M0 cap E(C_i) cap E(A,B) and N_i = (E(C_i) minus M0) cap E(A,B). They are disjoint with nonempty union (C_i has a cut edge), so P_i != N_i. (3) By vertex-disjointness, sig(M_S) cap E(C_i) = N_i if i in S and P_i otherwise. (4) For S != S', pick i in the symmetric difference; the signatures differ on E(C_i) by (2). (5) Hence 2^r distinct signatures. Scope: cubic bipartite graphs, any balanced cut. Relation: weakens the S0015 side-changing hypothesis to 'cycle has a cut edge'.

label: S0001
statement: LEMMA (S-blowup-tw-identity, re-derivation, closes no obligation). For every finite graph G and integer d >= 1, let G[K_d] be the lexicographic product of G with K_d. Then tw(G[K_d]) = d(tw(G)+1) - 1. PROOF. Upper bound: take an optimal tree decomposition (T, {B_t}) of G of width k. Then (T, {B_t x [d]}) is a tree decomposition of G[K_d]: each bag has size d|B_t| <= d(k+1), every edge of G[K_d] lies inside some B_t x [d] because the copies of an adjacent pair are fully joined, and for each vertex (v, i) the nodes containing it form the same subtree T_v. Hence tw(G[K_d]) <= d(k+1) - 1. Lower bound: let (T, {B_t}) be any decomposition of G[K_d] of width w. For each vertex v of G let T_{v,i} (i in [d]) be the subtree of nodes containing copy (v,i). Copies of one vertex, and copies of two adjacent vertices, are pairwise adjacent in G[K_d], so every pair of their subtrees intersects. Subtrees of a tree have the Helly property, so all copies of v, and all copies of u and v for each edge uv, lie in a common node. Define B'_t = {v : all d copies of v lie in B_t}. Then (i) every edge uv of G lies in some B'_t, since u and v have all copies in a common bag; (ii) {t : v in B'_t} is the intersection of the d subtrees T_{v,i}, which is a nonempty subtree; so (T, {B'_t}) is a tree decomposition of G. Since the d copies of each vertex in B'_t are distinct vertices of B_t, d|B'_t| <= |B_t| <= w+1. So tw(G)+1 <= max_t |B'_t| <= (w+1)/d, i.e. w >= d(tw(G)+1) - 1. Both bounds together give equality. NOTE: this is the known fact that treewidth is multiplicative under clique blow-up; it is recorded for the manuscript's Lemma 10 check only.

statement: LEMMA (wiring-invariance of oracle circuits, sub-gap (iii)). Let C be a Boolean circuit with gates of fan-in at most beta, each gate either a fixed gate or an oracle gate with an arbitrary function of its inputs. Let W(C) be its wiring: the set of input-to-gate arcs and the input/output labels, with no gate functions. Let D(C) be the dependency digraph (vertices = inputs and gates, arc u->g iff u is an input of g). Then (a) D(C) depends only on W(C); (b) for any two oracle assignments O, O' on the same wiring, D(C_O) = D(C_O') as labelled digraphs; (c) any property P of digraphs closed under isomorphism satisfies P(D(C_O)) = P(D(C_O')) for all O, O'.
proof: (a) D(C) is defined from the arc set and the labels only; gate functions are not used. (b) Follows from (a), since equal wirings give equal labelled digraphs. (c) Equal labelled digraphs are isomorphic, so P agrees on them. QED. Consequence (the barrier test): if the width route proves a bound of the form S(C) >= phi(D(C)) for a function phi of the dependency digraph, then the bound holds for every oracle assignment on that wiring, which is the robustness property used by CHOPRS Thm 2 (B3-O). A bound that uses gate truth tables cannot be written as phi(D(C)). The identity of Thm 8 eq.22 and Lemma 10 eq.26 is a statement about the wiring of a fixed linear kernel: tw(D(K)) = tw(H_B). Replacing linear gates by oracle gates of fan-in <= N^eps changes the wiring (it removes the linear-overlap arcs), so the identity does not transfer by (a)-(c); this matches gap (ii).
scope: Pure definitional statement about wirings and dependency digraphs; no assumption on the kernel, on beta, or on the target (8). Holds for every finite circuit.

statement: REPAIR of S0007 (basis-consistent P_r). label: S0002
statement: Proof of (a): a clause is falsified by x iff each of its literals is false, which fixes the variable of each literal to a specific value. Falsifying all clauses of S is the conjunction of these fixings. If two fixings give one variable different values, no x satisfies them, so |Fal(S)| = 0. Otherwise the fixings determine exactly |V(S)| variables and leave n - |V(S)| free, giving 2^(n-|V(S)|). A tautological clause forces some variable to both values, so it gives 0, consistent with its empty falsification event. Proof of (b): for each x, 1[x satisfies F] = prod over i of (1 - 1[C_i falsified by x]). Expanding the product gives sum over S of (-1)^|S| prod over i in S of 1[C_i falsified by x] = sum over S of (-1)^|S| 1[x in Fal(S)]. Summing over all x in {0,1}^n and using the definition of Fal(S) gives (b).

structure.evidence: cm-0cbc6e8c0c0a4ef0: 400/400 seeded random CNFs (n in 3..7, m in 1..9, clause sizes 2 or 3) agree exactly with brute-force counting. This run is finite and does not prove the identity; the proof above does. Scope: elementary inclusion-exclusion. It closes no open obligation of Q-e988ea9656 and is not progress toward P vs NP. structure.lemma: Let F be a CNF over variables 1..n with clauses C_1..C_m (literals may repeat; tautological clauses allowed). For S subset of [m], let Fal(S) = {x in {0,1}^n : every clause in S is falsified by x}, and let V(S) be the set of variables occurring in clauses of S. Then (a) |Fal(S)| = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if no variable is forced to both values by the falsifying requirements of S, and |Fal(S)| = 0 otherwise; (b) #SAT(F) = sum over S subset of [m] of (-1)^|S| * |Fal(S)|.

statement: LEMMA (s=1 sparse hitting set, exact within Boolean weight<=d points). Let F be any field, t >= d >= 0, and let H = {1_P : P subset [t], |P| = d}, so |H| = C(t,d). label: S0013
statement:
statement: LEMMA (two-monomial Boolean hitting set). Let F be a field, t>=d>=1, and M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j). There exists a set H of at most r=ceil(2^(d+1)(ln(M+binom(M,2))+1)) points in {0,1}^t such that every nonzero multilinear polynomial f over F with at most two monomials and degree at most d has f(a) != 0 for some a in H. Proof: Index monomials by supports S subseteq [t], |S|<=d; there are M supports. For each support S impose requirement A_S: some sampled point contains S. For each unordered distinct pair S,T impose requirement B_ST: some sampled point contains exactly one of S,T. For a uniformly random Boolean point a, A_S holds with probability 2^(-|S|)>=2^-d. For B_ST, choose an element in the symmetric difference, and name the supports so that it belongs to S\T. The event that every element of S is 1 and that chosen element of T\S is 0 has probability 2^(-|S|-1)>=2^(-d-1); it implies S is contained in a and T is not. Thus each requirement fails on one sample with probability at most 1-2^(-d-1), and on r independent samples with probability at most exp(-r*2^(-d-1)). There are M+binom(M,2) requirements. By the union bound, the probability any fails is at most (M+binom(M,2))*exp(-r*2^(-d-1))<=exp(-1)<1. So a sample satisfying all requirements exists; deleting duplicate points preserves satisfaction. For f=c*x_S with c!=0, A_S gives f(a)=c. For f=c*x_S+c'*x_T with distinct S,T and nonzero coefficients, B_ST gives a point where exactly one monomial evaluates to 1, so f(a) is c or c', nonzero over every field. Scope: existence only, multilinear degree<=d, at most two monomials; no polynomial-time construction claim or implication for general circuits. The size is O(2^d log M).

Proof: Index the possible monomials by supports S subseteq [t] of size at most d. For each S require that some sampled point a has S subseteq supp(a). For each unordered pair of distinct supports, name them S,T so T\S is nonempty, choose i in T\S, and require a point with S subseteq supp(a) and i notin supp(a). A uniform random Boolean point meets a single-support requirement with probability 2^(-|S|)>=2^-d. It meets the pair requirement with probability 2^(-|S|-1)>=2^(-d-1), since the coordinates of S and i are distinct. There are R=M+binom(M,2) requirements. With r independent samples, each requirement fails with probability at most exp(-r*2^(-d-1)); the union bound gives failure probability at most R exp(-r*2^(-d-1))<=exp(-1)<1. Thus a sample meeting all requirements exists; deleting duplicate points preserves them. For f=c*x_S, c!=0, a hit gives f(a)=c. For f=c*x_S+c'*x_T with distinct supports and both coefficients nonzero, the pair requirement gives x_S(a)=1 and x_T(a)=0, so f(a)=c. If like supports are combined or a coefficient is zero, the polynomial is a one-monomial case. This works over every field. Scope: existence only, multilinear polynomials with at most two monomials and degree at most d; no efficient construction claim and no general-circuit PIT consequence. The size is O(2^d log M).

statement_start: LEMMA (degree-two multilinear Boolean hitting set). Let F be any field and t>=1.
statement: LEMMA (degree-two multilinear Boolean hitting set). Let F be any field and t>=1. Every nonzero multilinear polynomial p(x)=a_empty + sum_i a_i x_i + sum_{i<j} b_ij x_i x_j over F has a nonzero evaluation on H={0,e_i (1<=i<=t), e_i+e_j (1<=i<j<=t)}. Proof: If p vanishes at every point in H, evaluation at 0 gives a_empty=0. Evaluation at e_i then gives a_i=0 for each i. Evaluation at e_i+e_j gives a_empty+a_i+a_j+b_ij=0, hence b_ij=0 for every pair. Thus all coefficients vanish, contradicting that p is nonzero. Therefore H hits every nonzero polynomial in this class. Its size is 1+t+binom(t,2). The argument works in every characteristic. This is a bounded subclass result and gives no general circuit-PIT or P-vs-NP consequence.

statement: LEMMA (bounded-degree multilinear Boolean evaluations determine coefficients). Let F be any field and 0<=d<=t. label: S0020
statement: statement: LEMMA. Let F be any field and t>=d>=1. Put M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j). Every nonzero multilinear polynomial f in F[x_1,...,x_t] of degree at most d is nonzero at some Boolean point whose set of 1-coordinates has size at most d. Hence the M points 1_A for A subseteq [t], |A|<=d, form a hitting set for this class. Proof: Index rows and columns by subsets A,S of [t] of size at most d, ordered by nondecreasing size (with the same order within each size). The evaluation matrix has entry x_S(1_A)=1 iff S subseteq A. If |S|>|A| the entry is zero. Within each equal-size block, containment holds iff S=A, so that block is the identity. Thus the matrix is block lower triangular with identity diagonal blocks and is invertible over F. The evaluations of f are this matrix times its coefficient vector; a nonzero coefficient vector cannot map to zero. Exact scope: all fields, multilinear polynomials, degree at most d; the bound is M evaluations and gives no sub-dimension PIT improvement.

label: S0021
statement: statement: LEMMA (sharp unrestricted linear case). Let F be any field and t>=1. The minimum cardinality of a set H subseteq {0,1}^t such that every nonzero multilinear polynomial f(x)=a_0+sum_{i=1}^t a_i x_i over F is nonzero at some point of H is exactly t+1. Upper bound: take H={0,e_1,...,e_t}; if f vanishes on H then f(0)=a_0=0 and f(e_i)=a_0+a_i=0, so each a_i=0. Lower bound: for any H of size r, the evaluation map from the (t+1)-dimensional F-vector space of affine multilinear polynomials to F^r is linear. If r<t+1 it has a nonzero kernel element, a nonzero polynomial vanishing on all of H. Thus the minimum is t+1. This is exact and constructive for degree at most 1 with unrestricted sparsity; it makes no PIT claim for general circuit classes.

statement: statement: LEMMA (minimum Boolean hitting-set size for unrestricted low-degree multilinear polynomials). Let F be any field, t>=1 and 0<=d<=t. Let V_{t,d} be the F-vector space spanned by monomials x_S=prod_{i in S}x_i for S subseteq [t], |S|<=d. The minimum cardinality of H subseteq {0,1}^t such that every nonzero f in V_{t,d} has f(a)!=0 for some a in H equals M=sum_{j=0}^d binom(t,j). Proof: dim(V_{t,d})=M. Evaluation on the full Boolean cube is injective: if f vanishes on all points, its multilinear coefficients are recovered by Möbius inversion on the subset lattice, so f=0. Hence the evaluation functionals for points in the cube span V_{t,d}^*; choose M of them forming a basis, and their evaluations detect every nonzero f. Conversely, fewer than M evaluation functionals give a linear map V_{t,d}->F^r with nonzero kernel, so no such H detects every nonzero f. Scope is all fields, Boolean points, unrestricted coefficients and sparsity; this is an existence/minimum-size result, not an efficient construction or PIT speedup.

statement: statement: For every field F and integers t,d,q>=1, let H={1_A in {0,1}^t: |A|<=min(qd,t)}. Every nonzero multilinear polynomial f in F[x_1,...,x_t] of degree at most d with at most q nonzero monomials is nonzero at some point of H. Thus H is a hitting set of size sum_{i=0}^{min(qd,t)} binom(t,i). Proof: write f=sum_{j=1}^k c_j x_{S_j}, where 1<=k<=q, each c_j!=0 and the S_j are distinct subsets of [t] of size at most d. Put U=union_j S_j, so |U|<=qd. All variables outside U are absent, and |U|<=t. The restrictions of the distinct monomials x_{S_j} to {0,1}^U are linearly independent as functions over F: if their linear combination vanished at every Boolean point, then its multilinear polynomial would be the zero polynomial, by induction on |U| (write g=g_0+x_u g_1; evaluations at x_u=0 and 1 force g_0=g_1=0), contradicting at least one c_j!=0. Therefore some assignment a in {0,1}^U has f(a)!=0. Extend a by zeros on [t] minus U; its support A has size at most |U|<=min(qd,t), so the extended point belongs to H and still has f(a)!=0. The displayed size counts all subsets A of size at most min(qd,t). Scope is arbitrary fields, multilinear polynomials, degree at most d, sparsity at most q; this is an explicit enumeration, not a polynomial-time PIT guarantee when qd grows.

statement: LEMMA (bounded-sparsity Boolean witness). Let F be any field and let f in F[x_1,...,x_t] be a nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree at most d with at most q nonzero monomials. Then there exists a in {0,1}^t with Hamming weight at most min(qd,t) such that f(a) != 0. Proof: Let U be the union of the supports of the monomials of f. There are at most q supports and each has size at most d, so |U| <= min(qd,t). The polynomial f depends only on coordinates in U. A multilinear polynomial in |U| variables that vanishes on all Boolean inputs is identically zero: induct on |U|, writing f=g+x_i h; evaluations at x_i=0 imply g vanishes everywhere and hence g=0 by induction, while evaluations at x_i=1 then imply h vanishes everywhere and hence h=0. Since f is nonzero, some Boolean assignment to U has nonzero evaluation. Extend that assignment by zero outside U; its value remains nonzero and its weight is at most |U|. The full set of points of weight at most min(qd,t) is therefore an existential hitting set for this class, of size sum_{j=0}^{min(qd,t)} binom(t,j). This step is a bounded mathematical lemma, not a polynomial-time PIT algorithm and not a closure of the general-circuit PIT obligation.

statement: For every field F and integer t≥1, there is an explicitly constructible set H⊆{0,1}^t of at most ceil(log2(t+1))+1 points such that every nonzero multilinear polynomial of degree at most 1 with at most two nonzero monomials is nonzero at some point of H. Construction: assign each variable a distinct nonzero binary codeword of length r=ceil(log2(t+1)); include the all-zero point and, for each codeword coordinate, the point whose 1-coordinates are exactly variables whose codeword has a 1 there. Proof: a nonzero constant is detected at the zero point; each variable is detected in some coordinate row. For a constant plus a variable, the zero point isolates the constant. For two distinct variables, their distinct codewords differ in a coordinate, whose row sets exactly one of the two variables to 1, isolating its nonzero coefficient. Thus the evaluation is nonzero over any field. The points are generated in O(t log t) time. This is an explicit hitting set for the stated sparse degree-one class only.

statement: Lemma (Boolean evaluation interpolation through degree d). Let F be any field, t>=0, and 0<=d<=t. Let P_d={1_A : A subseteq [t], |A|<=d}, where 1_A is the Boolean incidence vector. statement: LEMMA U (upper bound, width theorem). Setting as in the owner lower-bound text (steps i-iv, S0009). Let (T,beta) be a tree decomposition of G of width k = tw(G). Let tau1 = (1,2,0) and tau2 = (0,1,2) in T (both sum to 0 mod 3; independent; their supports {1,2} and {2,3} meet in colour 2). For v in V and i in {1,2}, let b(v,i) in K_G be the element whose vertex part is tau_i at v and 0 elsewhere; its edge part is forced by k(e,c) = -(k(u,c)+k(w,c)). Restriction to vertex coordinates is an isomorphism K_G -> T^V, and the vertex parts of the b(v,i) form a basis of T^V, so B_T = (b(v,i)) is a basis of K_G. Support of b(v,i): coordinates (v,c) and (e,c) for edges e at v, with c in supp tau_i. Two basis vectors share a coordinate iff (a) they have the same vertex v (they share (v,2)), or (b) their vertices u,v are adjacent in G (they share (uv,c) for c in supp tau_i meet supp tau_j, nonempty by L2); nonadjacent distinct vertices share nothing. Hence H_{B_T} = G x K2 (strong product: each vertex blown up to a 2-clique, adjacent blocks fully joined). Tree decomposition of H_{B_T}: replace each bag beta(t) by beta(t) x {1,2}. Each (v,i) lies in exactly the nodes containing v (connected). An in-block edge lies in the bag of v. A cross edge (u,i)(v,j) with uv in E lies in some beta(t) containing u and v, hence in beta(t) x {1,2}. The width is at most 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. So min over bases of tw(H_B) <= 2tw(G)+1. With the owner lower bound (every basis has tw(H_B) >= 2tw(G)+1), w*(F(G)) = min_B tw(H_B) = 2tw(G)+1 exactly, relative to the spec's definition of tw(H_B). Status: CLAIMED, needs review by a session of a different model family. No barrier claim is made: this is a width fact about coefficient graphs of kernel bases; it is not a circuit or proof-size lower bound and does not transfer to P vs NP. statement: For every finite simple graph G, tw(G[K_2]) = 2*tw(G)+1, where G[K_2] has vertex set V x {0,1} and (a,i)~(b,j) iff ab in E(G) or (a=b and i!=j). SCOPE: this is a statement about the fixed graph G[K_2] only. It does NOT bound min over bases of the coefficient graph of K_G, so it does not close G0001 or S0018.
derivation: UPPER BOUND: let (T,beta) be a tree decomposition of G of width k=tw(G). Set beta'(t)=beta(t) x {0,1}. Every edge (a,i)(b,j) of H has a=b (then a in beta(t) for some t, so both ends lie in beta'(t)) or ab in E (then a,b lie in a common bag). For each a, {t : (a,i) in beta'(t)} = {t : a in beta(t)} is connected, so beta' is a tree decomposition of H with bags of size at most 2(k+1), i.e. width at most 2k+1. LOWER BOUND: by Seymour-Thomas take a bramble B of G of order k+1. Let F = {B x {i} : B in B, i in {0,1}}. Each B x {i} is connected in H (edges (a,i)(b,i) for ab in E). Two members touch: if B, B' share a vertex a, then (a,i) and (a,j) lie in them and are equal or adjacent; if B, B' are joined by an edge ab of G with a in B, b in B', then (a,i) ~ (b,j) in H for any i,j. So F is a bramble of H. If X hits every member of F, then X_i = {v : (v,i) in X} hits every B in B for i=0 and i=1, so |X_i| >= k+1 and |X| >= 2(k+1). Hence the bramble order of H is at least 2k+2, and by Seymour-Thomas tw(H) >= 2k+1. Both bounds together give tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1. The same argument gives tw(G[K_n]) >= n(tw(G)+1)-1 with the matching upper bound by n-fold bag blow-up. STATUS: CLAIMED; the author is claude-haiku-5-5 and cannot review its own step. statement: LEMMA W-F (width theorem over an arbitrary field F). Let G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph, V nonempty, and let K_G^F subset F^I be the homogeneous kernel: (V) k(v,1)+k(v,2)+k(v,3)=0 for all v; (E) k(e,c)=-(k(u,c)+k(w,c)) for e={u,w}, all c. Then min over all bases B of K_G^F of tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G)+1, where H_B is the coefficient graph (j~k iff some coordinate is nonzero in both b_j and b_k). PROOF. Lower bound: the owner's Steps (i)-(iv) (LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md, sec. 1) go through verbatim over F. The only arithmetic inputs are: (L1) T={t in F^3: t1+t2+t3=0} has dim 2, and every nonzero t in T has at least two nonzero entries, since a single nonzero entry cannot sum to 0; (L2) any two subsets of {1,2,3} of size >=2 intersect (2+2>3). Steps (i)-(iv) use only these, linear algebra, and Fact (C). Hence tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1 for every basis B. Upper bound: put tau1=(1,-1,0), tau2=(0,1,-1) in T. Both have supports {1,2},{2,3}, which meet only in colour 2 and both entries there are nonzero. They are independent (a*tau1+b*tau2=0 forces a=0 by coordinate 1 and b=0 by coordinate 3). For v in V, i in {1,2}, let b(v,i) have vertex part tau_i at v, zero at other vertices, and edge part forced by (E). Restriction to vertex coordinates is an isomorphism K_G^F -> T^V, so B_T={b(v,i)} is a basis. Coordinates of b(v,i): (v,c) for c in supp tau_i, and (e,c) for e at v with c in supp tau_i (the edge part of b(v,i) on e is -tau_i(c)). Then (v,i)~(u,j) in H_B iff u=v (common coordinate (v,2)) or uv in E (common coordinate (uv,2)). Non-adjacent distinct vertices share no coordinate, since an edge coordinate lies only on edges incident to the vertex. So H_B = G[K_2] (each vertex replaced by a pair, complete between pairs of adjacent vertices and inside each pair). For a tree decomposition (T,beta) of G of width k, the bags beta(t) x {1,2} form a tree decomposition of H_B of width 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. So min_B tw(H_B) <= 2 tw(G)+1. Together with the lower bound: min_B tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G)+1. SCOPE: any field F, finite simple G, the homogeneous 3-colour kernel only (not the affine solution set, not the non-linear two-value condition). ORIGIN: generalises the owner's GF(3) proof; the 'arbitrary-field version' of Q-fbfe10bfb3 is addressed here by hand. BARRIER CHECK: not a circuit or proof-system lower bound for P vs NP; no barrier analysis required. STATUS: CLAIMED, hand-checked by the claimant only (same family as the reviewers); novelty against Kashyap (0711.1383) and Hlinený-Whittle still open (Q-f0f8a3a9f1).

statement: UPPER BOUND (claimed by claude-haiku-5-5 session, unreviewed). Setting: G=(V,E) finite simple, V nonempty, GF(3) homogeneous kernel K_G of the positive exact-one encoding with coordinates (v,c) and (e,c), c in {1,2,3}. CLAIM: (1) each b(v,i) lies in K_G; (2) B* is a basis of K_G; (3) the coefficient graph H_{B*} equals G[K_2] (vertices (v,i), adjacent iff v=u with i!=j, or uv in E); (4) hence min over bases of tw(H_B) <= tw(G[K_2]) <= 2 tw(G)+1. statement:
statement_start: For every n>=1, threshold t, variable order, and level k, the OBDD width of f(x)=[sum_i x_i >= t] at level k is at most k+1.
proof: Fix the first k variables in the chosen order. For any assignment a to them, let j(a) be its number of 1s. On the remaining variables y, the residual is f_a(y)=[j(a)+sum_i y_i>=t]=[sum_i y_i>=t-j(a)]. Hence residuals are determined by j(a) in {0,...,k}; there are at most k+1 distinct residual functions, which is exactly the OBDD width at level k.

statement:
statement_start: For every n>=1, nonnegative integer weights w_1,...,w_n<=W, integer threshold t, variable order, and level k, the OBDD width is at most kW+1.
statement: For every n>=1, nonnegative integer weights w_1,...,w_n<=W, integer threshold t, variable order, and level k in {0,...,n}, the Boolean threshold function f(x)=[sum_i w_i x_i >= t] has at most kW+1 distinct residual functions after fixing the first k variables in that order. Consequently its ordered binary decision diagram has size at most sum_{k=0}^n (kW+1)=W*n*(n+1)/2+n+1, hence polynomial size when W is polynomially bounded in n.
derivation: Fix a variable order and a level k. For any assignment alpha to the first k variables, let s(alpha) be the sum of w_i alpha_i over those variables. The residual on the remaining variables y is [sum_{i remaining} w_i y_i >= t-s(alpha)]. Since each fixed weight is an integer in [0,W], s(alpha) is an integer in [0,kW]. Thus there are at most kW+1 possible values of s(alpha), and assignments with the same value produce identical residual functions. The width at level k is therefore at most kW+1. Summing these width bounds over k=0,...,n gives the stated size bound. This argument covers zero weights and thresholds outside the attainable range as well.

statement: Lemma (Corrected Sparseness Bound): For every constant c >= 1, the number of truth tables on N = 2^n inputs computable by fan-in-2 circuits of size s = n^c is at most 2^{o(N)}. Proof: description length s*(4 + 2*log2(n+s)) + log2 s = 2s*log2(n+s) + O(s) = O(n^{c+1} log n) = o(2^n) = o(N).

statement: statement: Lemma (conditional deterministic-to-randomized inclusion). Fix an input length N and resource bounds T(N), S(N). Let K_det be a class of deterministic one-pass streaming machines for a fixed language L whose machines use at most T(N) time and S(N) space on every length-N input. Let K_rand contain randomized one-pass streaming machines under the same resource bounds, where deterministic behavior is allowed by ignoring the random tape. If a refuter R outputs, for every machine A in K_rand, an input y on which A errs (under the stipulated refuter quantifiers), then R also refutes every machine in K_det. Proof: For each A in K_det, define A' in K_rand with the same transition function and output, independent of its random tape. It uses the same resources and has identical output on every input, so any y witnessing error of A' witnesses error of A. This implication preserves the refuter's own uniformity and resources because R is unchanged. It applies only when K_det embeds with the same input-length indexing and resource bounds; it does not construct R or establish that K1 is contained in CJSW's resource-bounded class.

statement: Residual-state lower bound. Let L be any language over {0,1}, let k be a cut position, and let R_k be the set of distinct suffix languages L_p={z : |z|=N-k and pz in L}, as p ranges over {0,1}^k. Every deterministic one-pass machine that decides L on length-N inputs must have at least |R_k| distinct states after reading k bits, and therefore at least ceil(log2 |R_k|) state bits. Proof: If prefixes p,p' with distinct residual languages reached the same state, there would be a suffix z accepted after one prefix and rejected after the other. Starting from the same state, the deterministic transition/output behavior on z is identical, contradicting correctness. Thus distinct residual languages require distinct states; taking logarithms gives the bit bound.
evidence: Direct proof by indistinguishable-state contradiction; applies to exact deterministic one-pass decision at a fixed length and cut. No K1-specific value of |R_k| is established, so this lemma does not prove the K1/CJSW resource match or close G0001.

label: S0007
statement: statement: Search-to-decision implication for fixed-length MCSP streams. Fix a truth-table input length N and a circuit-size threshold s. Suppose a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm A, on every N-bit truth table x, outputs either (i) a circuit C of size at most s whose truth table equals x, or (ii) a distinguished failure symbol; suppose it outputs a circuit in case x has one of size at most s, and outputs failure otherwise. Then there is a deterministic one-pass decision algorithm D for MCSP[N,s] with the same state set, transition function, input order, and update-time bound as A, and with no greater working space: D runs A and accepts exactly when A's final output is a circuit. Proof: By the two output guarantees, A outputs a circuit exactly on members of MCSP[N,s]. D can use A's final output tag as its answer, without inspecting or retaining the input stream. Hence its streaming resources are unchanged. This implication does not establish that K1's algorithm satisfies these output guarantees in CJSW's precise parameterized model, nor does it provide the CJSW constructive refuter.

structure.gap: This narrows the search-versus-decision issue: any K1 search lower bound follows from a decision lower bound when search has the stated exact success/failure contract. G0001 remains open; next required work is checking the K1 length/resource parameterization against CJSW and establishing its refuter premise.

label: S0008
statement: Lemma (bounded-query deterministic simulation). Let M be a deterministic one-pass streaming machine whose per-input-symbol update performs at most q(N) adaptive oracle queries, each of length at most L(N), with non-oracle work at most T(N) per update and working space at most S(N), including the state used to generate each query. Let D be a deterministic decider for the oracle language, running in time U(L) and space V(L) on queries of length L. Then M can be simulated as a deterministic one-pass machine with per-symbol update time at most T(N)+q(N)(cL(N)+U(L(N))) and working space at most S(N)+cL(N)+V(L(N))+O(log(q(N)+1)), for an absolute constant c, plus the unchanged output storage of M. Proof: On each input symbol, simulate M's non-oracle instructions. Whenever it issues a query y, copy y into a buffer of at most L bits, run D on that buffer using V(L) scratch bits, feed the answer to M, erase/reuse the scratch and buffer, and continue. Adaptivity causes no extra storage because queries are processed sequentially and each next query is generated from M's current simulated configuration and the preceding answers. Each query costs O(L)+U(L) time, and the buffer and D workspace are reused, giving the stated bounds. Input is consumed only by M's original one-pass updates, so no rereading is introduced. This lemma does not imply that a Sigma_3SAT oracle is in P under P=NP, nor that CJSW's refuter premise applies to K1; it isolates the cost once a suitable deterministic oracle decider is actually available.

statement: Finite residual-row characterization (constructive). Let A be any subset of {0,1}^N and 0<=k<=N. For each prefix p in {0,1}^k define its residual row r_p in {0,1}^{2^(N-k)} by r_p(z)=1 iff pz is in A. Then a deterministic one-pass machine deciding membership in A has at least |{r_p}| states after k input bits, and a machine with exactly |{r_p}| states at that cut suffices for the remaining suffix decision if its state stores the row index. Proof: For the lower bound, if p,p' have different rows, some suffix z has r_p(z) != r_p'(z); a deterministic machine in the same state after p and p' would behave identically on z, contradiction. For sufficiency, map each prefix to its row class; on the next bit b, update row r_p to the class of r_{pb}, which is well-defined because equal rows imply for every b and suffix z that r_p(bz)=r_p'(bz), hence r_{pb}=r_{p'b}. At k=N the row is the single membership bit, so these transitions decide A exactly. This proves the residual-state characterization directly and does not use any earlier claimed step or give a K1-specific asymptotic bound.

label: S0010
statement: For each N>=1, let L_N={0^N} over {0,1}^N. At a cut k, the number r_k of distinct residual suffix languages is r_0=1 and r_k=2 for every 1<=k<=N. Proof: At k=0 there is only the empty prefix, whose residual is {0^N}. Fix k>=1. The prefix 0^k has residual {0^(N-k)} (the singleton containing the empty string when k=N). Every other length-k prefix has empty residual, since it already disagrees with 0^N. Both residuals occur, so there are exactly two. Consequently every exact deterministic one-pass decider for L_N has at least one state bit after every nonempty prefix cut: distinct residuals must reach distinct states, since a suffix distinguishing the residuals would otherwise receive the same deterministic continuation from the shared state. This is an exact residual-state result for the singleton language only; it supplies no growing lower bound and does not establish a resource match to CJSW for general MCSP.

label: S0011
statement: Explicit-candidate residual tracker. Let F be any fixed, explicitly listed subset of {0,1}^N with M=|F|, and let the stream be x_1,...,x_N in order. There is a deterministic one-pass machine with M state bits whose state after t bits is exactly the indicator vector v_t indexed by F, where v_t(f)=1 iff f[1..t]=x_1...x_t. Initialize v_0 to the all-ones vector. On bit b at position t+1, update each coordinate by v_{t+1}(f)=v_t(f) AND [f[t+1]=b]. By induction on t, this is precisely the set of listed strings extending the observed prefix. At the end, the stream belongs to F iff the state has at least one 1. The update takes O(M) Boolean operations and the description stores F in O(MN) bits (or read-only program constants); the machine uses M mutable state bits. Moreover, two prefixes induce the same state iff they have the same intersection of F with their extension cylinder, so this construction explicitly represents the residual candidate set for F. It gives a finite-list construction only: if F is the set of size-at-most-s circuit truth tables, its explicit listing can be exponentially larger than an MCSP decision circuit, and this lemma does not provide a polynomial-in-|H_C| update rule.

label: S0012
statement: Residual-count bound for a fixed-length candidate family. Let N>=0 and F be any finite subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=k<=N and each prefix p in {0,1}^k, define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-k}: pz in F}, and let r_k be the number of distinct sets R_p (including the empty set). Then r_k<=min(2^k, 2^{|F|}). Proof: there are exactly 2^k possible prefixes, so there are at most 2^k residual sets. Each residual is a subset of F under the bijection z -> pz, hence there are at most 2^{|F|} possible residuals. Taking the smaller bound proves the claim. Moreover, the candidate-subset tracker is exact: after prefix p it stores V=F intersect {pz:z in {0,1}^{N-k}}, identified with its suffixes; on next bit b it replaces V by {z: bz in V}. Induction on k proves the invariant, and at k=N, V is nonempty iff the input belongs to F. This is only a state-count upper bound and an explicit-list procedure; it gives no succinct update bound for circuit-defined F or CJSW resource match.

label: S0013
statement: Residual-count bound by family size, with a trie consequence. Let N>=0 and F be a fixed subset of {0,1}^N of size M. For 0<=k<=N define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-k}: pz in F} for each p in {0,1}^k, and let r_k count distinct such sets, including the empty set. Then r_k<=min(2^k,M+1). Proof: There are 2^k prefixes. For the second bound, each distinct nonempty residual R has at least one witness word x=pz in F whose prefix p induces R. Choose one such witness for each distinct nonempty residual. Witnesses chosen for different residuals are distinct, because a word x has a unique length-k prefix and hence belongs to only that prefix's residual; if the same x witnessed two residuals, those residuals would both equal R_p. Thus there are at most M distinct nonempty residuals, plus at most one empty residual. For the constructive consequence, build the prefix trie of F, with a rejecting sink for prefixes outside the trie. It has at most 1+NM nodes, recognizes F exactly, and each input-bit transition follows one child pointer or enters the sink, so after construction transitions take O(1) pointer operations. This does not bound construction, storage, or transition cost polynomially in a succinct circuit description of F, so it does not close the CJSW/MCSP bridge.

label: S0014
statement: Corrected explicit-trie bound. Let N>=0 and F be an explicitly listed subset of {0,1}^N with |F|=M. Its prefix trie has at most 1+NM nodes: the root contributes one, and each of the M words adds at most N nodes. Add one rejecting sink, if needed, for every missing child transition. The resulting deterministic automaton has at most NM+2 nodes, recognizes F exactly, and each transition takes O(1) pointer operations after construction. Proof: a word reaches its terminal trie node exactly when all its bits follow trie edges; any missing edge enters the rejecting sink, which loops on both symbols. The node bound follows by charging each non-root trie node to a word having that prefix, with at most N charged nodes per word, then adding the root and at most one sink. This is an explicit-list construction and gives no polynomial resource bound from a succinct circuit description of F.

statement: Disjoint-residual bound. Let N>=0, F be a finite subset of {0,1}^N, and 0<=k<=N. For each length-k prefix p define R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-k}: pz in F}, and let r_k be the number of distinct R_p, including the empty set if it occurs. Then r_k<=min(2^k, |F|+1). Proof: There are 2^k prefixes, so r_k<=2^k. For distinct prefixes p,p' of equal length, R_p and R_p' are disjoint: a suffix z in both would make the same string have two different length-k prefixes. Thus the nonempty distinct residuals are pairwise disjoint subsets of F. Each contains at least one element of F, so there are at most |F| nonempty residuals. There is at most one additional empty residual, proving r_k<=|F|+1. This sharpens the generic 2^{|F|} subset bound. It is a structural state-count bound only; for succinctly specified MCSP candidate families it gives no polynomial bound unless |F| itself is polynomial.

statement: Layered one-hot residual transition circuit. Let N>=0 and L be any subset of {0,1}^N. For 0<=k<=N, let R_k be the set of distinct residual languages R_p={z in {0,1}^{N-k}: pz in L} over prefixes p of length k, and put r_k=|R_k|. There is a deterministic layered one-pass automaton with one-hot state at each level k, recognizing L exactly, whose transition circuit for input position k has fan-in-2 Boolean circuit size O(r_k+r_{k+1}). Proof: At level k use one bit x_R for each R in R_k, with exactly the current residual bit set. For b in {0,1}, define R_b={z:bz in R}; this is a member of R_{k+1}. For each R' in R_{k+1}, set its next-state bit y_{R'} = OR over all (R,b) with R_b=R' of (x_R AND [input=b]). There are exactly 2r_k source/input pairs; forming the gated terms costs O(r_k), and ORing the terms by destination costs O(r_k+r_{k+1}) total including empty destinations. The initial state is the unique residual at k=0. At level N accept iff the active residual contains the empty string. Induction on k proves that the active state is the residual of the read prefix, hence the automaton accepts exactly L. The circuits may depend on k and L; the claim makes no uniform construction-cost assertion.

statement: statement: Lemma (oracle elimination under P=NP). Let O be any language in PH and suppose P=NP. Then O is decidable by a deterministic polynomial-time machine. Consequently, a deterministic one-pass streaming machine with polynomial per-symbol work apart from at most polynomially many adaptive O-queries of polynomial length can be simulated by a deterministic one-pass machine with polynomial per-symbol update time and polynomial space, provided its own non-oracle update and query-generation work and space are polynomially bounded. Proof: P=NP implies coNP=NP=P. Inductively, if Sigma_i^P=Pi_i^P=P, then Sigma_{i+1}^P=NP^{Sigma_i^P}=NP^P=NP=P, and likewise Pi_{i+1}^P=P; thus PH=P and O has a deterministic polynomial-time decider. For an input stream of total length N, process each query sequentially using that decider, erase and reuse its query buffer and workspace, and return its answer before continuing the adaptive update. If the decider uses time polynomial in query length L and space polynomial in L, then each update takes T(N)+q(N)·poly(L(N)) time and S(N)+poly(L(N))+O(log(q(N)+1)) space, which remain polynomial. This preserves one-pass input access and determinism. The statement is conditional on P=NP; it supplies no constructive refuter and does not by itself imply K1 lies in a CJSW class.

statement: statement: Length-sensitive sequential oracle simulation. Let M be a deterministic one-pass machine with S(N) working bits and at most T(N) non-oracle update steps per input symbol. If an update adaptively issues queries y_1,...,y_r to a fixed oracle language O, and O has a deterministic decider using time U(ell) and space V(ell) on inputs of length ell, then the update can be simulated with time T(N)+sum_i(O(|y_i|)+U(|y_i|)) and space S(N)+max_i(O(|y_i|)+V(|y_i|))+O(log(r+1)). Proof: simulate M until it issues a query; copy that query to a buffer, run the decider, return its answer, and reuse the buffer and decider workspace for the next query. Adaptivity is preserved because each answer is returned before the next query is generated. Summing per-query running times proves the time bound. Sequential reuse means only the largest query buffer and decider workspace are simultaneously live, proving the space bound. M consumes the input in its original one-pass order. This resource lemma supplies neither the K1/CJSW parameter embedding nor a constructive refuter; G0001 remains open.

statement: Repair of the bounded-query deterministic simulation lemma. Let M be a deterministic one-pass streaming machine whose per-symbol update makes at most q(N) adaptive oracle queries, each of length at most L(N), with non-oracle update time at most T(N) and working space at most S(N), including query-generation state. Let D decide the oracle language, and let U(ell), V(ell) bound its time and space on every query of length exactly ell. Define U_<=L(N)=max_{0<=ell<=L(N)} U(ell) and V_<=L(N)=max_{0<=ell<=L(N)} V(ell). Then M can be simulated with per-symbol update time at most T(N)+q(N)(cL(N)+U_<=L(N)) and working space at most S(N)+cL(N)+V_<=L(N)+O(log(q(N)+1)), for an absolute constant c, plus unchanged output storage. Proof: Simulate M's ordinary instructions and process each generated query sequentially. Store each query in an L(N)-bit buffer and run D on it using at most V_<=L(N) scratch bits and U_<=L(N) time; reuse both buffer and scratch for subsequent adaptive queries. Query generation uses M's current simulated configuration and previous answers already retained in M's state, so adaptivity adds no query-sized accumulation. At most q(N) queries occur, giving the time bound; the reusable buffer and decider workspace give the space bound. M still consumes each input symbol once. This corrects S0008's missing monotonicity hypothesis. It is a generic simulation lemma and does not close the K1/CJSW resource-match gap.

statement: For every finite L subset of {0,1}^N and cut k, the minimum number of deterministic one-pass recognizer states after k bits is exactly the number of distinct residual rows r_p(z)=1 iff pz is in L. The upper bound is realized by storing the residual-row class; transitions are well-defined because equal rows have equal restrictions to either next bit. The lower bound follows because distinct rows have a suffix on which they differ, so they cannot reach the same state.
proof: For the upper bound, use one state per residual-row equivalence class at each level. On reading bit b, send class [r_p] to [r_{pb}]. If r_p=r_q, then for every suffix z, r_{pb}(z)=r_p(bz)=r_q(bz)=r_{qb}(z), hence the target class is independent of the representative. At level N the residual row is the single membership bit, which determines acceptance. For the lower bound, if p and q have different rows, choose z with r_p(z) != r_q(z). If the machine reached the same state after p and q, deterministic processing of z would give the same outcome, contradicting correct recognition.

statement: Let C be a finite subset of {0,1}^N and L=C. At every cut k, the number of distinct residual rows r_p(z)=1 iff pz is in L is at most |C|+1. Hence the residual-class recognizer uses at most ceil(log2(|C|+1)) state bits at every cut.
proof: For a prefix p, its row is nonzero exactly when some x in C extends p. If two distinct nonzero rows r_p and r_q contained the same x, then x would have both p and q as its length-k prefix, impossible. Thus the number of nonzero rows is at most |C|. All zero rows coincide, so there is at most one additional row. The residual-class recognizer stores one class index and has one state per distinct row, giving the stated bit bound.

statement: Residual-state upper bound for circuit MCSP. Fix n>=1, s>=0, N=2^n. Use topologically ordered circuits with constants, input literals, fan-in-two AND/OR/NOT gates, and size equal to gate count. Let L_{n,s} be the length-N truth tables computed by circuits of size at most s, and B=4(n+s+2)^2. At every cut k, the number of distinct residual suffix languages of L_{n,s} is at most min(2^k, 2^(2^(N-k)), 1+(s+1)B^s). Proof: A j-gate circuit description has at most four gate types and at most (n+j+2)^2 ordered source pairs per gate, so there are at most B^j descriptions. Thus |L_{n,s}|<=sum_{j=0}^s B^j<=(s+1)B^s. For each length-k prefix p, let R_p={z:pz in L_{n,s}}. There are at most 2^k prefixes and at most 2^(2^(N-k)) possible residual subsets. Also, the nonempty residuals are at most |L_{n,s}|: choose one accepted full string from each nonempty residual; strings chosen for distinct prefixes are distinct because their length-k prefixes differ. This proves the bound. Residual languages give a deterministic automaton: the transition on bit b maps R_p to R_{pb}, which is well-defined because equal residuals agree on every suffix beginning with b. Therefore the bound also upper-bounds the minimal state count. It does not bound the time to compute or update a residual class, so it does not establish the CJSW resource match or close G0001.
evidence: Direct circuit-description count and residual-language argument given in the statement. The conclusion is an upper bound on state count only; efficient transition computation remains open.

statement:
statement: Explicit residual automaton for a listed finite language. Let N>=0 and let A be an explicitly listed subset of {0,1}^N, with M=|A|. For each k=0,...,N, define R_{k,p}={z in {0,1}^{N-k}: pz in A} for p in {0,1}^k. At each cut k there are at most M+1 distinct residual sets, and a deterministic layered automaton deciding A can be constructed from the list using O(N(M+1)) states and O(N(M+1)) transitions, with O(1) transition lookup time after construction. Proof: At a fixed cut, every nonempty residual R_{k,p} contains at least one word x in A with prefix p. Choose one such x for each distinct nonempty residual. Words chosen for different residuals have different length-k prefixes: a word x has only one such prefix, and therefore can be assigned to only one residual. Hence the number of nonempty residuals is at most M; include the empty residual to get at most M+1. For transitions, if R_{k,p}=R_{k,p'}, then for each bit b and suffix z of length N-k-1, bz belongs to R_{k,p} iff p'bz belongs to A, equivalently z belongs to R_{k+1,pb}; the same equivalence holds for p', so R_{k+1,pb}=R_{k+1,p'b}. Thus the transition from a residual class on b is well-defined. Enumerate prefixes at each level, compute their residuals by scanning the listed words, merge equal residuals, and store each class's two successor class identifiers. This gives the stated state and transition counts and constant-time table lookup. Construction time is polynomial in N and M (for example O(N^2 M) with direct prefix comparisons). The lemma does not imply an efficient uniform construction for MCSP because its accepted truth-table list may be too large to enumerate.

statement: statement: Lemma (MCSP completion-profile state bound). Fix n,s and let E_{n,s} be the set of length-2^n truth tables computed by Boolean circuits of size at most s. For 0<=k<=2^n and each prefix p in {0,1}^k define R_p={z in {0,1}^{2^n-k}: pz is in E_{n,s}}, and let w_k be the number of distinct sets R_p. Every deterministic one-pass machine that decides MCSP[n,s] on length-2^n truth-table inputs has at least w_k states after k bits. Proof: if p,p' have different residual sets, choose z in their symmetric difference. Then exactly one of pz,p'z is in E_{n,s}. If the machine reached the same state after p and p', its deterministic behavior on the common suffix z and final decision would agree, contradicting correctness. Hence distinct residual sets require distinct states.

statement: Constructive residual-row automaton lemma (general finite-language form). The induced transition on a bit b maps [p] to [pb], which is well-defined because equality of r_p and r_q implies equality after restricting both rows to suffixes beginning with b. At k=N, each row is the membership bit, so the layered residual-class automaton decides A exactly. The induced transition on a bit b maps [p] to [pb], which is well-defined because equality of r_p and r_q implies equality after restricting both rows to suffixes beginning with b. At k=N, each row is the membership bit, so the layered residual-class automaton decides A exactly. Proof: If r_p=r_q, then for every suffix z, pz∈A iff qz∈A, so their residual languages agree; conversely, distinct rows differ at some suffix and therefore have different residual languages. For well-definedness, if r_p=r_q, then for every remaining suffix z, r_{pb}(z)=r_p(bz)=r_q(bz)=r_{qb}(z), hence r_{pb}=r_{qb}. The final one-bit rows give acceptance. This is a constructive structural lemma only; it gives no K1-specific lower bound and does not close the CJSW bridge.

statement: Candidate A clauses 1-4 are jointly unsatisfiable for any admissible exact deterministic one-pass algorithm A, given Thm 4.1 of PNP-001-PAPER-BASIS-BLOWUP-v4.0 and monotonicity of treewidth under subgraphs. Proof: fix G=G_{m,s}, K=K_{m,s}, d, A, B=B_A. By clauses 1-2, Thm 4.1 gives G[K_d] as a subgraph of H_B. Treewidth is monotone under subgraphs, so tw(H_B) >= tw(G[K_d]) = d(tw(G)+1)-1 =: LB, which does not depend on A. Clause 3 gives tw(H_B) <= F(m,s,S_A,U_A). Hence LB <= F. Clause 4 asserts LB > F for the same parameters and resource bounds. Contradiction. Scope: this refutes the conjunction of clauses 1-4 as stated, not any single clause. label: S0003
statement: LEMMA L1 (inclusion-exclusion for #F, for a CNF F over variables x_1..x_n, each clause c a set of literals (v,s) with c satisfied iff x_v = s). Let N(S) = 2^(n-|V(S)|) if the requirement map req_S(v) = 1-s (over all literals (v,s) in clauses of S) is single-valued, and N(S) = 0 otherwise, for S a subset of the clauses of F. Then #F = sum over S subset of clauses of (-1)^|S| N(S). PROOF: #F = sum over x in {0,1}^n of prod_c [x satisfies c], and [x satisfies c] = 1 - [x falsifies c], where x falsifies c iff x_v = 1-s for every literal (v,s) of c. Expanding the product gives prod_c (1 - f_c(x)) = sum_S (-1)^|S| prod_{c in S} f_c(x), where f_c = [x falsifies c]. prod_{c in S} f_c(x) is the indicator that x_v = req_S(v) for all v in V(S) (and is 0 if req_S is not single-valued, since then no x satisfies all of them). The number of x with prescribed values on V(S) is 2^(n-|V(S)|) when consistent. Summing over x and exchanging the sums gives the identity. Check: a clause containing both (v,0) and (v,1) is always satisfied; its falsification set is empty, and the consistency test returns N=0 for every S containing it, which matches. Finite check: cm-271be1be38e94fc9 (400 random CNFs, n<=5, 0 mismatches; the control without the consistency test gives 218 mismatches).

statement: statement: For every finite graph G and integer d >= 1, the lexicographic blow-up H = G[K_d] (each vertex v becomes a clique of d copies, and copies of adjacent vertices are fully adjacent) satisfies tw(H) <= d*(tw(G)+1) - 1. Proof: let (T, {X_t}) be a tree decomposition of G of width tw(G). Set X'_t = X_t x [d]. Vertices: each copy v_i lies in X'_t for every t with v in X_t. Edges: a copy-internal edge v_i v_j lies in any X'_t containing v; a cross edge u_i v_j with uv in E(G) lies in X'_t for any t with {u,v} in X_t. Connectivity: {t : v_i in X'_t} = {t : v in X_t}, a subtree of T. Bag sizes are at most d*(tw(G)+1), so the width is at most d*(tw(G)+1) - 1.

label: S0022
statement:
Lemma (General Blow-up Treewidth Bound for Restricted Candidate A). Let G be a finite nonempty simple graph, F a field, d ≥ 1 an integer, and K ⊆ F^I a linear space with block partition {X_v : v ∈ V} satisfying conditions (R), (L), (E) with parameter d. Let B be any finite spanning family of K, and let H_B be its support-overlap graph. Then tw(H_B) ≥ d·tw(G) + d - 1 = d(tw(G)+1)-1.

Proof. 
1. By Theorem 4.1 (Abstract Embedding Theorem, PNP-001-PAPER-BASIS-BLOWUP-v4.0.md pp. 4-5), under conditions (R), (L), (E), the graph G[K_d] is isomorphic to a subgraph of H_B. The theorem states: "for every finite spanning family B = (b_j)_{j∈J} of K there is an injection ι: V × {1,...,d} → J that maps every edge of G[K_d] to an edge of H_B. In particular G[K_d] is isomorphic to a subgraph of H_B."

2. Treewidth is subgraph-monotone: if H ⊆ H_B is a subgraph, then tw(H) ≤ tw(H_B). (Section 2 of the paper: "Both parameters are subgraph monotone.")

3. By Lemma 2.2 (Width of the Blow-up, p. 3), for every nonempty graph G and every d ≥ 1, tw(G[K_d]) = d·tw(G) + d - 1 = d(tw(G)+1)-1. The proof is elementary: upper bound by blowing up a decomposition of G, lower bound by projecting a decomposition of G[K_d] back to G and using disjointness of the cliques Q_v = {v} × {1,...,d}.

4. Combining (1)-(3): tw(H_B) ≥ tw(G[K_d]) = d·tw(G) + d - 1.

Application to restricted Candidate A: For the colouring kernel K_{m,s} = K_{G_{m,s}}(F) with d=2 (Proposition 5.2, p. 5), any spanning family B_A that is a spanning family of a linear space satisfying (R),(L),(E) with d=2 satisfies tw(H_{B_A}) ≥ 2·tw(G_{m,s}) + 1. This corrects the citation in S0019 from Corollary 6.2 (the d=2 special case) to the general Lemma 2.2.

statement:
statement: For every finite deterministic automaton A=(Q,Σ,δ,q0,λ) with m states and λ:Q→{0,1}, over any field F there is an exact linear representation of its transitions on F^m: encode q as e_q, set T_a e_q=e_{δ(q,a)}, and read output by y(e_q)=λ(q).
proof: Induction on word length. Initially the vector is e_q0. If after w it is e_{δ*(q0,w)}, applying T_a gives e_{δ(δ*(q0,w),a)}=e_{δ*(q0,wa)}. The output functional returns λ(δ*(q0,w)), exactly the automaton output. Thus transitions and outputs are represented exactly for every word.
scope: Finite deterministic automata; representation dimension m; arbitrary field F.

label: S0027
statement:
statement: For a finite deterministic automaton A=(Q,Σ,δ,q0,λ) with output f(w)=λ(δ*(q0,w)), let r_q(w)=λ(δ*(q,w)) for reachable states q and V=span_F{r_q}. The minimum dimension d of any linear representation f(w)=y(T_w v0), with one linear transition T_a per symbol a and T_w the corresponding product, equals dim_F V.
proof: For the upper bound, define T_a r_q=r_{δ(q,a)} on generators. This extends well-definedly: if Σ_q c_q r_q=0, then for every suffix w, Σ_q c_q r_{δ(q,a)}(w)=Σ_q c_q r_q(aw)=0. Set v0=r_{q0} and y(g)=g(ε). Induction gives T_w v0=r_{δ*(q0,w)}, so y(T_wv0)=f(w), in dimension dim_F V. For the lower bound, any d-dimensional representation induces the linear map Φ:F^d→F^{Σ*}, Φ(v)(w)=y(T_wv). For every prefix u, its residual function w↦f(uw) equals Φ(T_u v0). Therefore all residual functions, and hence their span V, lie in im Φ, whose dimension is at most d. Thus d≥dim_F V; combined with the construction, the minimum is dim_F V.
scope: Finite deterministic automata; arbitrary field F; only linear representations with a fixed initial vector, one linear transition per input symbol, and a linear output functional.

label: S0028
statement:
statement: For a finite deterministic automaton A with output f:Σ*→F, the row space over F of its Hankel matrix H_f indexed by prefixes u and suffixes v, with H_f(u,v)=f(uv), equals the span of its reachable residual functions r_u(v)=f(uv). Consequently its Hankel rank equals the minimum dimension of a fixed-transition linear representation f(w)=y(T_w v0).
proof: Each Hankel row indexed by u is the function v↦f(uv), exactly the residual function after prefix u. Prefixes reach states of A, and every reachable state has a prefix reaching it, so these rows are precisely the residual functions of reachable states. Their linear spans and dimensions agree. A finite automaton has finitely many reachable states, so this span is finite dimensional. By the minimum-dimension characterization in S0027, the common dimension is the minimum linear representation dimension.
scope: Finite deterministic automata over a finite alphabet, outputs in a field F; the Hankel matrix may be infinite but has finite rank. The representation consequence is only for a fixed initial vector, one linear transition per symbol, and linear output functional.

statement:
statement: For the explicit two-state DFA with transitions δ(q0,0)=q0, δ(q0,1)=q1, δ(q1,0)=δ(q1,1)=q1, initial q0, and outputs λ(q0)=1, λ(q1)=0, the DFA is minimal but its Hankel matrix over F_2 has rank one.
proof: q0 and q1 are both reachable (by ε and 1), and they are distinguishable by suffix ε since their outputs differ; hence this accessible DFA is minimal. For any suffix v, the residual from q1 is zero because q1 is absorbing with output 0. The residual from q0 equals 1 exactly if v contains only zeros, and is nonzero at ε. Every prefix reaches q0 or q1, so the Hankel rows are precisely this nonzero residual and the zero residual. Their F_2-span has dimension exactly one.
scope: One explicitly specified finite DFA; alphabet {0,1}; output field F_2.

statement_start: Lemma (Linear Candidate A Lower Bound). Let A be an admissible exact deterministic one-pass algorithm for MCSP^A[s] whose state evolution is linear (maintains a linear subspace of F_2^N updated by linear transformations). Suppose there exists a linear space K_{m,s} satisfying (R),(L),(E) with parameter d >= 1, and a spanning family B_A of K_{m,s} representing the states of A. Then tw(H_{B_A}) >= d(tw(G_{m,s})+1)-1. Consequently, if the algorithm's resource bound F(m,s,S_A,U_A) < d(tw(G_{m,s})+1)-1, the algorithm cannot exist.
derivation: Proof:
1. By assumption, K_{m,s} satisfies (R),(L),(E) with parameter d >= 1 (Clause 1).
2. By assumption, B_A spans K_{m,s} (Clause 2).
3. Theorem 4.1 (Abstract Embedding) applies: since (R),(L),(E) hold, there exists an injection from V x {1,...,d} to the index set of B_A mapping edges of G[K_d] to edges of H_{B_A}. Thus G[K_d] is isomorphic to a subgraph of H_{B_A}.
4. Treewidth is monotone under subgraphs: tw(H_{B_A}) >= tw(G[K_d]).
5. By Corollary 6.2 of PNP-001-PAPER-BASIS-BLOWUP-v4.0 (verified for small cases in cm-0df22e2ced824471), tw(G[K_d]) = d(tw(G)+1)-1.
6. Therefore tw(H_{B_A}) >= d(tw(G_{m,s})+1)-1.
7. If the algorithm's resource bound implies tw(H_{B_A}) <= F(m,s,S_A,U_A) (Clause 3), then F >= d(tw(G)+1)-1.
8. Clause 4 asserts d(tw(G)+1)-1 > F for all MMW-admissible parameters and resource bounds.
9. Hence for linear algorithms, Clauses 3 and 4 cannot both hold; any such algorithm must violate its claimed resource bound.

Scope: This lemma applies exactly to the class of linear streaming algorithms for MCSP^A[s] (state evolution = linear subspace updated by linear transformations). It does not apply to nonlinear algorithms (branching, AND gates, polynomial state encodings), for which no linear K with (R),(L),(E) exists modeling their state transitions (refutation of original S0002, cm-9752c6603cd44ae3).

statement: statement_start: Lemma (Clause 3 Failure for Nonlinear Algorithms). Let A be the nonlinear streaming algorithm for MCSP^A[s] with degree-3 polynomial state encoding over F_2, where state evolution is p <- p * x_new + x_new (mod 2, degree <= 3). There exists no linear space K_{m,s} over F_2 satisfying properties (R), (L), (E) of Theorem 4.1 (PNP-001-PAPER-BASIS-BLOWUP-v4.0) and a spanning family B_A of K_{m,s} that represents the state evolution of A. Consequently, Clause 3 of Candidate A is false as stated, because it quantifies over EVERY admissible exact deterministic one-pass algorithm A, but for this nonlinear A, the required map A -> B_A does not exist. Proof: The reachable state set R_A is an algebraic variety not closed under addition, while any linear space K is closed under addition. No linear K can model nonlinear state evolution. This refutes Clause 3's universal quantification. Open question: whether any alternative definition of A -> B_A (without linear K, (R),(L),(E)) could work for nonlinear algorithms.
