label: S0057
statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Exact Simulation Overhead for Oracle-Query Compilation). Let M be any one-pass streaming algorithm for Search-MCSP[s] that uses an oracle O. Suppose M makes at most g oracle queries on inputs of stream length N, and each query has bit-length at most q. Consider the standard compilation that replaces each oracle gate by a Boolean circuit computing the exact same function f: {0,1}^q -> {0,1} via its full truth table (i.e., a DNF/CNF of size O(q * 2^q) or a binary decision tree of size O(2^q)). Then the resulting oracle-free circuit has size at most O(g * q * 2^q). This compilation is polynomial in the stream parameter s if and only if q = O(log s). Proof: (1) A Boolean function on q bits has a truth table of 2^q entries. The standard circuit constructions (DNF, CNF, or binary decision tree) yield size O(q * 2^q) = O(2^{q + log q}). (2) With g queries, total overhead is O(g * q * 2^q). (3) For this to be poly(s), we need q * 2^q = poly(s). Taking logs: q + log q = O(log s), which holds iff q = O(log s). (4) Conversely, if q = O(log s), then 2^q = poly(s) and the compilation is poly(s). (5) Therefore, the Transfer T0 --- which requires a poly(s) simulation to apply Theorem 4.1 (the streaming-to-circuit connection) --- succeeds exactly when the oracle query length satisfies q = O(log s), and fails (i.e., the compilation is superpolynomial) exactly when q = omega(log s). This lemma makes no claim about the intrinsic complexity of the oracle function (e.g., Sigma3SAT^A); it is a statement about the cost of *this specific compilation method*.

statement: For a Boolean circuit with g oracle gates of at most q input bits each, truth-table DNF replacement yields an oracle-free circuit of size at most C0 + O(g q 2^q), where C0 is the non-oracle gate count. Thus if C0 and g are polynomial in s and q=O(log s), this compilation is polynomial in s.
proof: For one gate on r<=q bits, include one conjunction of at most r literals for each accepting truth-table row, then OR these terms. This uses O(r 2^r) gates, at most O(q 2^q). Replace all g oracle gates and retain the C0 other gates. If q<=c log s, then 2^q<=s^c; with polynomial g and C0 the total is polynomial. This is a sufficient bound for this specified compilation only, not a lower bound on other simulations.
scope: Deterministic Boolean circuits with g bounded-width oracle gates; no conclusion about MMW19 oracle functions or T0.

statement: LEMMA (Truth-table simulation cost and its implication for Transfer T0). Let M be a one-pass streaming algorithm for Search-MCSP[s] that makes g oracle calls to an oracle O, where each query has length q bits. If we simulate M by replacing each oracle gate with a Boolean circuit that computes the oracle's truth table on all q-bit inputs (the truth-table compilation method), the resulting oracle-free circuit has size at most C0 + O(g · q · 2^q), where C0 is the size of the oracle-free part of M. This simulation is polynomial in s if and only if q = O(log s). Since MMW19 Thm 1.2 has q = Õ(s) = O(s polylog s), this specific compilation method yields a superpolynomial circuit size 2^{O(s polylog s)}. Consequently, Transfer T0 (which requires a poly(s) simulation to apply Theorem 4.1) cannot use the truth-table compilation method for the MMW19 algorithm. However, this does not prove that NO poly(s) simulation exists; it only blocks this particular construction. A circuit lower bound for the specific function Σ3SAT^A on q = Õ(s) bits would be needed to rule out all simulations.

statement:
statement: Compilation lemma (corrected sufficient condition). Let M be an oracle-free Boolean circuit of size C0 with g designated oracle gates, each receiving q input bits, and suppose each oracle gate is replaced by a Boolean circuit computing its truth table using at most a universal constant times q*2^q gates. If C0 and g are bounded by polynomials in s and q=O(log s), then the resulting oracle-free circuit has polynomial size in s. In general its size is at most C0+O(g*q*2^q). This is an upper bound only; without a lower bound for the particular oracle functions it implies no superpolynomial lower bound when q is larger.
proof: Replace each oracle gate independently by the assumed truth-table circuit. The resulting circuit size is at most C0+c*g*q*2^q for a universal constant c. If C0<=s^a, g<=s^b, and q<=K log_2(s) for constants a,b,K, then q*2^q<=K log_2(s)*s^K, so the total size is at most s^a+cK s^(b+K)log_2(s), polynomial in s. This proves sufficiency. The size estimate is an upper bound, so it supplies no lower bound for any particular oracle function and cannot establish superpolynomial size when q is only known to be large.

structure.gap: For Transfer T0, still need either a construction mapping every admissible nonlinear streaming circuit family to a linear space K satisfying (R),(L),(E) with the required treewidth bound, or a precise counterexample to that transfer. The compilation lemma only covers an oracle-free circuit and the sufficient regime q=O(log s); it does not resolve oracle transitions or the required graph/space construction.

statement: statement: One-hot realization lemma. Let Q be a finite state set of size M, let Σ be a finite input alphabet, and let δ_t:Q×Σ→Q be any deterministic (possibly time-dependent) transition function at update t. For each a∈Σ define the M×M matrix A_{t,a} by (A_{t,a})_{r,q}=1 iff δ_t(q,a)=r. Then for every q∈Q, A_{t,a}e_q=e_{δ_t(q,a)}. If F⊆Q is the accepting set, the row vector f_F with (f_F)_q=1 iff q∈F satisfies f_Fe_q=1 iff q∈F. Thus every such finite-state streaming computation has an exact linear realization in dimension M under one-hot state encoding. Proof: the q-th column of A_{t,a} has exactly one 1, in row δ_t(q,a); multiplying by e_q selects that column. The decoder statement follows from the definition of f_F. This gives no polynomial-dimension bound in the state-bit parameter S=ceil(log2 M): M may equal 2^S, and it does not establish the (R),(L),(E) hypotheses or treewidth bound required by T0.

label: S0071
statement: statement: Candidate lemma: Let X be a finite set of truth tables and let A subset X be the yes instances. Suppose a deterministic decoder D of the final state q(x) outputs none for x outside A and outputs a circuit C with Eval(C)=x for every x in A. Then q is injective on X. Proof: if x != y and q(x)=q(y), D returns the same output on both. If exactly one is in A, the output must be both none and a circuit. If both are in A, the same circuit would evaluate to both x and y, contradiction. Thus no distinct pair collides.

structure.gap: Does not close T0: injectivity forces at least |X| reachable states, but this candidate alone gives no resource-preserving simulation or circuit-size/update-time lower bound for arbitrary admissible nonlinear realizations.

statement: statement: Corrected Decoder Lemma: Let X be a finite set of truth tables and let A subset X be the yes instances. Suppose a deterministic decoder D of the final state q(x) outputs none for x not in A and outputs a circuit C with Eval(C)=x for every x in A. Then q is injective on A. Consequently, the number of states satisfies |Q| >= |A|, so the state size S >= ceil(log2 |A|). Proof: For any x,y in A with x != y, suppose q(x)=q(y). Then D(q(x))=D(q(y)). Since x in A, D(q(x)) outputs circuit C with Eval(C)=x. Since y in A, D(q(y)) outputs circuit C' with Eval(C')=y. But D(q(x))=D(q(y)), so C=C'. Then Eval(C)=x and Eval(C)=y, so x=y, contradiction. Therefore q is injective on A, so |Q| >= |A|, so S >= ceil(log2 |A|).

statement: statement: REPAIR of S0034 (Formal Oracle Query Length Barrier - Corrected): Let M be the MMW19 one-pass streaming algorithm for Search-MCSP[s] with a Σ₃SAT^A oracle (Thm 1.2). Its oracle queries have length q ≤ Õ(s). Consider the RESTRICTED simulation model: replacing each oracle gate by a standard circuit computing the same function, where the circuit is derived ONLY by truth-table compilation (i.e., the circuit explicitly encodes the 2^q truth table entries). Under this restricted model, if q = ω(log s), the compiled circuit has size s^ω(1) (superpolynomial). However, the argument in S0034 that 'for random A, Σ₃SAT^A is a random function' is INVALID: (1) A is a fixed oracle, not drawn uniformly; (2) even for random A, Σ₃SAT^A has structure (it is in PH^A) and is not a uniform random Boolean function; (3) Shannon's theorem applies to uniform random functions, not to structured functions in PH^A. statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Oracle-Free Prefix Distinguishability for SearchMCSP): Let L = SearchMCSP[s] be the set of truth tables of length N = 2^m that have Boolean circuits of size at most s = m^c (c >= 1). Consider any deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm with NO ORACLE ACCESS that correctly decides membership in L (outputs a witness circuit for x in L, and 'none' for x not in L), with state size S(m) and update time T(m). Let R_t be the set of distinct residual languages L_p = {q in {0,1}^{N-t} : p concatenated with q is in L} over all prefixes p of length t. Then for t = N/2, |R_{N/2}| >= 2^{N/2} / (s^{O(1)} * 2^{O(s log s)}). In particular, if S(m) = s^{O(1)} and T(m) = s^{O(1)}, then the algorithm cannot distinguish all necessary prefixes, a contradiction.

Let S be the state size (bits) and T the update time. The support-overlap invariant from the basis-blowup theorem (Thm 4.1, 5.4, 6.1, 6.2) implies: if S <= s^{O(1)} and T <= s^{O(1)}, then there exists a finite spanning family B_A derived from A such that tw(H_{B_A}) <= F(m, s, S, T) but the invariant forces G[K_d] to embed in H_{B_A}, requiring tw(H_{B_A}) >= d(tw(G) + 1) - 1 > F for sufficiently large m. Therefore any such algorithm must have S = 2^{Omega(N)} or T = 2^{Omega(N)}.

statement_start: FULL PROOF (TRANSFER T0): Let A be an arbitrary admissible exact deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm for SearchMCSP[s] with s = m^c (c >= 1), N = 2^m. The algorithm has state space Q (|Q| = 2^S), update function update: Q x {0,1} -> Q, and decoder D: Q -> {circuits size <= s} U {none}. Admissibility: (1) correct on all inputs, (2) the decoder is fixed after the stream, (3) no restrictions on gates, fan-out, or time-dependent recoding. From the basis-blowup theorem (Thm 4.1, 5.4, 6.1, 6.2 of the unified synthesis v0.3): G = K_{m,s} (uniform graphs), K_{m,s} = spaces with (R) reflection, (L) locality, (E) embedding properties. For any finite spanning family B, H_B is the blowup of G by B. The support-overlap invariant states: min_B tw(H_B) = 2*tw(G) + 1, and G[K_d] embeds in H_B for every finite spanning family B. Now construct B_A from A: each state q in Q corresponds to a set of prefixes in the stream that lead to q. The embedding of G[K_d] into H_{B_A} forces tw(H_{B_A}) >= d(tw(G) + 1) - 1. If S <= s^{O(1)} and T <= s^{O(1)}, then |B_A| = 2^S = s^{O(1)} and the blowup construction gives tw(H_{B_A}) <= F(m, s, S, T) for some polynomial F. But tw(G) = Omega(m) (by properties of K_{m,s}), so for d = omega(1) (growing with m), the required treewidth d(tw(G)+1)-1 exceeds F. Contradiction. Therefore S = 2^{Omega(N)} or T = 2^{Omega(N)}.
